themes.label: Unauthorized transactions and denied fraud claims
themes.description: Consumers allege unauthorized withdrawals, scams, or account takeovers and claim the bank denied or inadequately investigated their fraud or dispute claims.

examples.summary: Consumer claims two withdrawals totaling $2,510 from their checking account were unauthorized, but the bank denied the fraud claim after investigation, determining the transactions were authorized, without providing detailed evidence or explanation to support that conclusion.

Consumer claims their bank account was hacked and approximately an unspecified amount of funds were withdrawn without authorization, and that multiple credit cards and personal devices were also compromised or stolen.

Consumer claims three unauthorized transactions totaling $1700 were made to their account through a spoofing scam impersonating the bank, and the bank failed to properly document all disputed transactions, backdate the claim to the original filing date, or expedite resolution despite the consumer's medical hardship.

themes.label: ATM and deposit not credited
themes.description: Consumers allege cash deposits, ATM transactions, or transfers were not credited or were mishandled and that disputes were not resolved or provisional credit was not issued.

examples.summary: Consumer claims three ATM transactions were deducted from account without funds being received, disputes were filed but provisional credit was not issued within the required timeframe despite multiple resubmissions and escalations.

Consumer claims a cash deposit of $180 was accepted by an ATM but not credited to their account, and that USAA denied their dispute twice without providing requested documentation despite the transaction being verifiable through ATM logs, camera footage, and card access records.

Consumer claims an ATM malfunction failed to credit a cash deposit while retaining the funds, resulting in loss of $1,860 and creating immediate risk of eviction and medical emergency for a dependent with a serious health condition.

themes.label: Account freezes, restrictions and closures
themes.description: Consumers allege accounts were frozen, restricted, or closed without adequate explanation, review, or timely resolution, leaving them without access to funds.

examples.summary: Consumer claims that a financial institution froze all accounts due to garnishment and refused to conduct a manual review of claimed exemption documentation or connect them with a supervisor or legal department despite an active judicial appeal.

A bank placed a fraud restriction on a consumer's account after a bill pay transaction, and despite the consumer verifying the transaction as legitimate, the account restriction remained in place for over a week with inconsistent communications and unmet resolution timelines.

Consumer claims a 20-year checking account was blocked after calling to resolve disputed transactions, with the bank requiring a notarized identity letter rather than digital authentication, causing bill payment failures and temporary account access denial.

themes.label: Service, accessibility, fees and communication issues
themes.description: Consumers allege poor service, inadequate accommodations, fee notice problems, bill pay errors, or unwanted communications in managing their accounts.

examples.summary: Consumer claims a bank employee was rude and neglectful while processing a deposit, leaving the consumer waiting without apology.

Customer with hearing loss claims Citibank denied access to security technology requiring phone activation, repeatedly disconnected IP relay calls, and refused to provide web-based chat for business customers, violating ADA accommodation requirements.

Consumer alleges a bank charged dormant service fees and reinstated monthly maintenance fees to an inactive account over approximately two years without providing effective notice via the consumer's active email address, instead using an outdated physical address for adverse disclosures while using the current email for other communications.

brief.headline: Steady high account-management complaints, led by fraud disputes and ATM deposit credit claims
brief.what_is_happening: Complaints in this cluster are elevated but not sharply accelerating. Velocity is 1.05 (rank 21 of 79), with recent monthly volume slightly above the baseline average. In a 40-narrative AI-reviewed sample, consumers claim unauthorized transactions were denied or inadequately investigated, ATM or deposit amounts were not credited, and accounts were frozen or closed with little explanation. These are unverified allegations. The sample is small and the summaries are AI-generated.
brief.who_is_affected: Checking and savings account holders across a broad set of banks, with no single company standing out. Complaints are concentrated in CA (14.2%), FL (10.1%), TX (9.4%) and NY (7.8%). The AI sample suggests 22.5% of sampled consumers may be vulnerable, such as those with medical hardship or dependence on protected funds, and mean severity is 3.83 of 5.
brief.likely_root_cause: Hypothesis to test: fraud and dispute investigations may be inconsistently documented or explained, and provisional credit timelines may not be met for ATM and deposit disputes. Automated fraud or garnishment restrictions may also be applied without a timely manual review path. Scam-driven account takeover (impersonation and spoofing) may be raising both claim volume and denial friction.
brief.process_or_control_to_check: Check the fraud and unauthorized-transaction dispute workflow: investigation documentation, denial-rationale communication, and provisional credit timing. Also check ATM deposit reconciliation and exception handling, plus the account restriction, freeze and closure review process, including manual review of garnishment exemption claims and escalation paths.
brief.regulatory_area: Electronic fund transfer error resolution and unauthorized transaction disputes, with secondary attention to account restrictions and closures and funds availability.
evidence: Recent monthly average is 4,545.33 complaints versus a baseline average of 4,328.83.
Monthly counts were 4,501 in June 2026, 4,580 in July 2026 and 4,555 in August 2026, versus 3,416 in September 2025.
Templated share of the 2,973 recent narratives is 0.0%.
Company lifts are close to parity: Navy Federal Credit Union 1.101, Capital One 1.071, Citibank 1.046, Wells Fargo 1.032, Bank of America 1.032, with no company materially above 1.

Of the 40 sampled narratives, 43.6% involve unauthorized transactions and denied fraud claims, 23.1% ATM and deposit not credited, 17.9% account freezes or closures, and 15.4% service, fees and communication issues.
AI-assessed mean severity is 3.83 out of 5, and 22.5% of the sample involve a vulnerable consumer.

checks.name: size
checks.reason: The brief attributes the signal to no single company, and the top company lifts range from 0.911 to 1.101 (Navy Federal 1.101, Capital One 1.071, Wells Fargo 1.032), so this is a market-wide pattern rather than a size artifact.

checks.name: templating
checks.reason: Templated share of the 2,973 recent narratives is 0.0%, well under the 30% threshold.

checks.name: concentration
checks.reason: The top state CA holds only 14.2% (FL 10.1%, TX 9.4%) and the top ten companies all have 371 to 1,494 complaints with lifts near 1, so it is not confined to one state or company.

checks.name: thin_evidence
checks.reason: The sample has 40 complaints and 2,973 recent narratives, and the fraud/unauthorized (43.6%), ATM/deposit (23.1%) and freeze/closure (17.9%) themes cover about 85% of the sample and match the named root causes.

checks.name: seasonality
checks.reason: Recent months of 4,501, 4,580 and 4,555 are stable with no single peak month carrying the 4,545 average, and the last two months have not fallen materially from the peak (4,555 vs 4,580).

skeptic.note: The brief survives all five checks: a broad, non-templated, sustained market-wide elevation with themes that fit the named root-cause hypotheses.
